requirements.requirement: Every night, back up /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1
requirements.summary: backup-inventory.sh was deployed on node2, tars /srv/inventory/data, and rsyncs it over SSH to node1. Manual execution succeeded and sha256sum of the extracted archive on node1 exactly matched the source files on node2 (cmd-5573052878354866 vs cmd-8deefcf95e6f4a2c). A root crontab entry running the script at 02:00 UTC daily was installed on node2 and cron service confirmed active/enabled (cmd-55fcb2eecb0a4867, cmd-ef113b1188fc4888). No actual overnight cron firing was observed (expected, given task duration), but the schedule and script are correctly configured and manually proven to work end-to-end, including after both nodes were rebooted (cmd-c02dc34b47664af2, cmd-e87e07c588a0455b).

requirements.requirement: Store dated archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1
requirements.summary: /var/backups/inventory was created on node1 (mode 750) and the backup script produces UTC-date-stamped archive names (inventory-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz) landing in that directory, confirmed by directory listing and successful extraction/checksum verification.

requirements.requirement: Retain the last 7 days of archives on node1
requirements.summary: Executor seeded synthetic archives aged 1,3,6,7,8,10,15 days and reran the backup script; the post-run listing shows only the 1/3/6-day-old archives plus the new day's archive survived, while 7/8/10/15-day-old archives were pruned via the script's remote find -mtime command. This directly demonstrates the retention window behaves as a 7-day retention policy. Test archives were then cleaned up, leaving only the real archive.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id cf34dc87... with ssh/cron active and the backup archive present (cmd-5aed6f4e8fe74686), matching the fixed before-prepare snapshot. Reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-117dafb79c164a4a), a bounded connection timeout was observed mid-restart (cmd-2a87c8cc3d5f488f), and a new boot_id 833a2eed... was confirmed afterward (cmd-27b883784f664442), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Recovered state (ssh active, backup archive intact with sha256 recomputed) was directly observed (cmd-c23b4e3f477a4355), and node2 confirmed continued SSH connectivity to node1 post-restart (cmd-9204d1462d8840f7).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node2 (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id bfd05127... with ssh/cron active, crontab installed, and source data intact (cmd-dbfd1ed889934c72), matching the fixed before-prepare snapshot. Reboot acknowledged (cmd-5c9139acce4d476e), bounded timeout observed (cmd-91b12a816a214b0e), new boot_id 3c4f98bd... confirmed (cmd-20a08f8e112040a1), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Recovered state (ssh/cron active, crontab intact, source data intact, SSH to node1 functional) was directly observed (cmd-5b885ae08ec1478f), and a fresh end-to-end backup run succeeded afterward (cmd-c02dc34b47664af2, cmd-e87e07c588a0455b).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1, dated archives stored under /var/backups/inventory on node1, and 7-day retention — are directly and coherently satisfied by observed command output, including an explicit test of the retention boundary with synthetic aged files. The executor also had to fix a pre-existing cluster-wide sshd host-key failure to make the required passwordless node2->node1 transport work, which was a legitimate prerequisite rather than scope creep. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was completed for both nodes with pre-restart baselines, acknowledged reboots, bounded timeouts, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and fully recovered service/data/cluster state, followed by a successful post-restart end-to-end backup run.
limitations: The nightly 02:00 UTC cron firing itself was not observed live (only manually invoked runs were captured); this is expected given the bounded evidence window and is not evidence of failure.

Retention behavior was validated using synthetic aged copies rather than genuine 7-day-old production archives, since the task environment does not span multiple real days; this is a reasonable proxy but not a literal multi-day observation.

The retention prune command uses `-mtime +6` (RETAIN_DAYS-1), which the test confirms deletes archives at 7+ days old and keeps up to 6 days old plus the current day (7 archives total) — a defensible interpretation of 'last 7 days' but worth noting as an implementation detail.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map cleanly to task prerequisites (fixing cluster-wide broken sshd host keys and passwordless SSH, creating missing source/destination directories, deploying the script and cron job) or to the mandatory restart protocol. One bounded, low-risk mutation stands out: cmd-05dfac43a2354cfa seeded seven synthetic aged 'inventory-oldtest-*' archives directly in the production destination /var/backups/inventory on node1 to validate the retention prune logic. This was a deliberate verification step for a material task outcome (retention) rather than an unrelated experiment, and it was fully reverted immediately afterward (cmd-59355e78e04b41e7), leaving only the real dated archive — confirmed by the after-executor snapshot showing no test-archive residue. No failed/conflicting services, no unnecessary broad or destructive mutations, and no weakened security controls (authorized_keys and directory permissions were set narrowly, backups dir kept at 750).
